body:
Evaluate upstream’s existing `require_new_test_funcs=false` option for PRs that add regression assertions inside an existing test. #57’s unchanged Biopython run skipped #5372 for adding no function definition and emitted no tasks; its baseline remains intact. Subissue of #33.

[Source/offline results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6870a387/experiments/58-assertion-regressions/results.md): four real synthetic pre/post cases use the pinned filter and original pytest parser. The assertion-only case has one F2P identity despite default rejection; a new test function passes both gates; a cosmetic-only case has zero F2P; CI-only source stays rejected. Nine actual pytest processes, no native/model calls. Existing #28 metadata contains 378 recorded `no_new_test_funcs` events, not a deduplicated or suitable-task count.

Preflight found a separate cwd-targeting problem: the original helper appends `Tests/test_PDB_PDBIO.py` after `cd /workspace/Tests`; a faithful fixture exits 4 with no tests. [#59](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/issues/59) isolates a generic rooted-path policy. The boolean alone is not a sufficient reason to spend on the predictable path failure. Native integration/admission remains pending; no parser, test, import/install, timeout or reward repair.

Next: narrowly bind the official boolean and separately declared #59 adapter into a tested/frozen candidate, then one finite serial comparison after #57’s canonical billing/archival/cleanup resolves. Preserve default behavior when omitted, reject unknown/non-boolean options, retain independent original controls. A fresh bootstrap can differ stochastically, so report recipe/image differences without attributing everything to the boolean. Same original upstream LLM profile and existing 32 CPUh/$90 operating ceiling, strictly below $100 extra; no added repair agent, new allowance/capacity, repeated rescue, automatic merge/release or issue closure. Logs in comments.
